hotspots.topic: System design narrative and scope of work
hotspots.whyItMatters: This handbook expands on NFPA 72's 'why,' which is useful for scope-and-intent style exam questions.
hotspots.cite: Handbook — confirm chapter in your copy; parallels the NFPA 72 fundamentals chapter
hotspots.trap: Memorizing a rule number without the design intent behind it, which is exactly what a scenario-style question tests.

hotspots.topic: Voice evacuation and mass notification basics
hotspots.whyItMatters: Expands on notification-appliance rules with voice/paging system context.
hotspots.cite: Handbook — confirm chapter in your copy; cross-check the NFPA 72 notification chapter
hotspots.trap: Treating a voice evacuation system as 'just louder speakers' instead of a zoned, intelligible-message system with its own performance criteria.

hotspots.topic: Interface with suppression and building systems
hotspots.whyItMatters: Fire alarm systems often trigger HVAC shutdown, door release, or elevator recall — cross-system interlocks show up on scenario questions.
hotspots.cite: Handbook — confirm chapter in your copy; cross-check the NFPA 72 protected-premises chapter
hotspots.trap: Assuming the fire alarm contractor 'owns' every interlocked device instead of recognizing which interfaces are coordinated with other trades.
